definitions.explanation: Excessive pride in one's appearance, achievements, or possessions, especially to impress others.

examples.japanese: {虚栄心|きょえいしん}から{高価|こうか}なブランド{品|ひん}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought expensive brand-name goods out of vanity.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{虚栄心|きょえいしん}が{強|つよ}い。
{虚栄心|きょえいしん}を{満|み}たすために{無理|むり}をする。
examples.english: To push oneself too hard to satisfy one's vanity.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{虚栄|きょえい} (vanity, empty glory) + {心|しん} (heart, mind) → vain heart = vanity

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{虚|きょ} - empty, false
・{栄|えい} - glory, prosperity
・{心|しん} - heart, mind

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{虚栄心|きょえいしん}が{強|つよ}い - to have strong vanity
・{虚栄心|きょえいしん}から - out of vanity
・{虚栄心|きょえいしん}を{満|み}たす - to satisfy one's vanity
・{虚栄心|きょえいしん}を{捨|す}てる - to abandon one's vanity

RELATED WORDS:
・{見栄|みえ} - show, pretense, vanity
・{見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る - to put on airs
・うぬぼれ - self-conceit
・{自尊心|じそんしん} - self-esteem (more neutral)

NUANCE:
{虚栄心|きょえいしん} is almost always used negatively, suggesting empty or false pride focused on superficial appearances.
